title: ElevenLabs to Invest Hundreds of Millions in India, Eyes Acquisitions
excerpt: The $22 billion voice-AI company's India bet: local teams, Indian-language models, and possible acquisitions — with India already its biggest market by signups.
body:
• ElevenLabs plans to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in India, co-founder Mati Staniszewski told Reuters on October 6, and is open to acquiring Indian companies.
  • The money will go toward local teams, AI model development, and Indian-language work; the exact figure was not disclosed.
  • India is already the voice-AI company's largest market by user signups and its second-largest by enterprise revenue.
  • The announcement caps a $22 billion valuation after a $300 million employee tender offer last week.

AI voice company ElevenLabs plans to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in India, co-founder Mati Staniszewski told Reuters on Tuesday, in one of the largest bets yet by a global AI lab on the country's voice-AI economy.

The investment will fund local teams, model development, and work on Indian languages, Staniszewski said. He added that the company is open to merger and acquisition targets in India but declined to name any. The company did not disclose the exact investment amount or a timeline.

Why India

India has become central to ElevenLabs' business. It is the company's largest market by user signups and its second-largest by enterprise revenue. Its latest text-to-speech model supports 14 Indian languages, and the company says it plans to cover all 22 officially recognized languages in the coming months.

Indian enterprises are already running on its platform at scale: Meesho automates more than 60,000 customer support calls a day in Hindi and English, Cars24 handles over 20,000 multilingual conversations a month, and Mahindra, TVS Motor Company, IDFC Bank, and JioStar are among its customers. The company says it has paid more than $1 million to Indian voice talent through its Voice Actor Marketplace and given free API access to over 500 Indian startups through its grants program. Its India team, currently around 18 people, is expanding.

A $22 billion company doubling down

Founded in 2022 by Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski, ElevenLabs was valued at $22 billion after a $300 million employee tender offer in late September backed by Wellington Management and T. Rowe Price — roughly double its $11 billion Series D valuation from February. The company says its platform now handles more than 15 million voice-agent conversations a week across 90-plus languages.

Separately on Monday, Karnataka's Innovation and Technology Society signed an agreement with ElevenLabs to explore voice-AI applications for public services, including accessibility and voice restoration — a sign of how quickly the company's India footprint is widening beyond commercial deals.
